content: Letter 22, to Amīr Fīrūzshāh (ca. 827-28/1423-24?, Yazd?): Ibn Turka is glad at the arrival of the royal troops in Persian Iraq under the amir's command, counting it a great boon to religious leaders and scholars who had been suffering from the region's unrest (except the nukabā-yi ḥirmān), and wishes to attend the amir's court at once but is prevented at the moment (TMN/M f. 51b, TMN/MS p. 18, TMN/D pp. 184-86). MK's footnote: Fīrūzshāh's family was assigned the governorship of Isfahan in 827/1424 or 828/1425.
